component.name: Open Task Manager
component.summary: See what is running and quit what is stuck

description.p: Open Task Manager is a fast, native system monitor. It shows every process as a flat list, a process tree, or grouped by owner, user or category, with the memory of each group summed up.

ul.li: Processes as a flat list or a tree, with folding and keyboard navigation
Dynamic filters with autocomplete for process, user, category, state, CPU and memory
Configurable columns: show, hide, reorder, resize and sort; the layout is saved
Multi-selection with Ctrl-click, Shift-click and Ctrl+A; actions apply to the whole selection
Overview with CPU, memory, network, disk, per-core load and system information
Right-click actions: quit, force quit, suspend and resume, copy details
Light and dark themes, text size and high-contrast options

description.p: Everything runs on this computer. Open Task Manager makes no network requests and sends no telemetry.

screenshot.caption: Every process with its app, CPU, memory and disk activity
The process tree, with branches that fold and unfold

ul.li: Select anything: group rows, tree sections and processes all join the selection (⌘/Ctrl-click, Shift-click, Shift+arrows, ⌘A); actions apply to every process inside the selected rows, never to macOS's own.
Filtering no longer locks the tree open: fold and unfold with the keyboard or the chevrons while filtering, and ↓ or Return from the filter field moves into the table.

Every table has every column feature: resize, double-click to fit, drag headers to reorder, show/hide, sideways scrolling, and a saved layout (Users, Startup Items, Services, Connections, Apps, Disk Space).
The Columns menu reorders by drag and drop.
Plain, shorter wording across the app: titles name things, explanations are gone.
Fixed: clicks in a Columns menu could reach the row underneath it.

Multi-selection in every table, desktop style: ⌘-click (or Ctrl-click) toggles, Shift-click selects a range, Shift+arrows extend, ⌘A selects all. Quit, Force Quit, Copy and the right-click menu act on the whole selection; listing pages get bulk Enable/Disable, Restart/Stop, Move to Trash (one confirmation) and Copy.
Autocomplete in every filter: each page suggests its columns' values (State, Scope, Protocol, Process, User…) as chips with counts.
Double-click a column divider to fit the column to its content.
Overlay scrollbars wherever content overflows: the process table (both directions), every listing table and the Overview, Power, Benchmarks, Settings, Disk Space and Recorder pages.
Group processes from a dropdown instead of a segmented control.
App icons in every table and on nearly every process (owner app, system icons, or the executable's own icon).
Holiday themes for 21 holidays, applied automatically around each date (Settings: Automatic, Off, or preview any).
Lucide icons replace every emoji and glyph in the interface, and the app logo sits next to its name.
Fixed: opening the Popout or the Screensaver crashed the app.
Dark-mode accent and holiday palettes meet WCAG 4.5:1 contrast.

description.p: Sortable, filterable tables everywhere, and a pass over the small details, checked against Apple's Human Interface Guidelines, WCAG 2.2 and published table, filter and dashboard guidance.

ul.li: Every table sorts by clicking a header (numbers by value, biggest first; click again to reverse), and every table filters on all of its columns: Users, Startup Items, Services, Connections, Installed Apps, and the Disk Space folders and scan history. Users is now a sortable table.

Force Quit asks first (Cancel is the default; Return and Esc cancel), single or bulk. Force Quit items sit apart from Quit in the right-click menu, and items that don't apply are hidden instead of dimmed.
Quit and Force Quit stay in the toolbar, dimmed without a selection, so it no longer shifts. Both are in the Edit menu too (Quit Process ⌥⌘Q). Pause Updates moved to ⌥⌘P, freeing ⌘P.

The filter field edits at a caret (←→, Home/End, ⌥⌫), Space types, ↓ opens suggestions, hovering moves the highlight, clicking a chip turns it back into text, and `cpu>` / `mem>` without a number says what to type.
Shortened text shows its full value on hover; paths keep their end ("…" in the middle).
Numbers use fixed-width digits so live values don't jitter; disk and file sizes use Finder's 1000-based units; per-process disk and network figures are true per-second rates; tiny values show "<1%".
Better contrast for secondary text, borders and selected rows (white text on a darker blue); a 2 px focus ring; larger click targets for chip and clear buttons; equal-width grouping buttons.
Notices carry ✓ or ⚠ as well as colour, errors stay 15 seconds, and copying says what was copied.
Empty tables say so (with Clear filter when filtering), "12 of 40 shown" while filtering, headers stay visible while a page loads, and arrow keys only scroll as far as needed.
The window title follows the page.
Native macOS system monitor in Rust and GPUI with Liquid-Glass styling.

Processes: flat list, process tree (operating system vs. your processes, grouped by subsystem and owner app), owner, user and category grouping; per-branch memory sums; batch folding; keyboard navigation.
Dynamic filters: autocomplete chips for app, user, category and state, plus `cpu>` and `mem>` thresholds.
Configurable, reorderable, resizable columns with horizontal scrolling; app icons.
Right-click actions: quit, force quit (with children), suspend/resume, show in Finder, show connections, copy.
Overview, Users, Connections, Power, Startup items, Services, Installed apps, Disk space, Benchmarks, Flight recorder, Settings, popout and screensaver.
Menu bar with update-speed controls and shortcuts.
A filter field with a caret and focus ring (⌘F), match counts while filtering, and an empty state with Clear filters; a two-row toolbar that never overflows; long names end in "…".
`otm --demo <scene>`: a fictional computer for screenshots and recordings; nothing real is read or signalled.
